citation.title: Development and validation of a predictive model for the pedestal height
citation.authors: P. B. Snyder, R. J. Groebner, A. W. Leonard, T. H. Osborne, H. R. Wilson

topic: EPED1 pedestal height/width model combining peeling-ballooning stability (ELITE, model equilibria) with a KBM-motivated width relation; validated on DIII-D.
own_question: Can pedestal height and width be predicted from eight engineering/global inputs before an experiment?
actual_method_and_evidence: Offline MHD stability scans plus an empirical width fit from 4122 DIII-D Thomson time slices. Comparison on 41 discharges gave predicted/observed height ratio 1.00±0.18. Inputs use measured pedestal density. Ti is set equal to Te in the model. There is no CES, BES/ECEI, or time-resolved nowcasting.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Pedestal-top pressure strongly influences H-mode performance, which motivates monitoring pedestal-top quantities.
claim_checks.qualification: Background motivation only. This is a steady inter-ELM model, not a source on ion temperature measurement.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Inputs are pre-shot or global parameters. The target is the pedestal maximum in the last 20% of the ELM cycle. The source does not address real-time timing.
validation_if_relevant: Prior predictions were tested in a dedicated DIII-D experiment, plus random database discharges. The source does not report data splits for the width-coefficient fit.
forbidden_inferences: Do not use this source to support carbon-impurity CES Ti nowcasting or BES/ECEI information.
Do not claim that EPED1 provides real-time estimates.
Do not treat its Ti=Te assumption as evidence about KSTAR ion temperature.
Do not generalize it to KSTAR without validation.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: It could optionally be cited as general pedestal-importance background. It has no bearing on the paper's methods, targets, or validation, so it can be omitted.
